learning: Sensing changes (span at iteration 1, y at iteration 2) each left line loss at about 1.0 per run. Mass is the next untested lever. If line loss persists at 0.6 kg, the next step is a wheel change (wheel_radius or wheel_track), not another sensing change.
notes: Single-change test of mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg on the iteration 2 geometry, with the controller held fixed. Expected: fewer line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom, and max_error under 0.06 m for longer. This is a hypothesis; the race has not measured it.
rationale: Iteration 2 showed that moving the sensors from y=0.04 to y=0.03 m left line loss at 1.0 per run on oval, s-bend and slalom (score 47.85). Iteration 1 showed that widening the span to ±3 cm did not remove it either. Sensing has now been changed twice without effect, and steering oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.13), so the robot is losing the line on bends, not jittering. Following the decision rule in the Builder's feedback, this iteration tests the dynamics lever: mass drops from 0.7 to 0.6 kg, with the sensor row, span, sensor size, wheel_track and wheel_radius unchanged. Yaw inertia scales with mass, so the lighter robot should turn more readily for the same wheel-speed difference. The controller is held identical to iteration 2 (kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction recovery, weights scaled to x), so any change in line loss can be attributed to mass. I expect line-loss events below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom. This is a hypothesis, not a measured result. Speed is not reduced, because a 3 s finish needs about 1.5 m/s average and the robot has not yet finished any run.
